purpose: Prove that regex, tree-sitter, SCIP, and LSP spellings of the SAME Java method overload normalize to one provider-neutral CanonicalFactKey, while distinct overloads of the same method name remain distinct keys.
notes: regex and tree-sitter spellings are GROUND TRUTH captured from the current semidx extractor (semidx.runtime.languages.java/parse-file with default opts).
SCIP and LSP spellings are REPRESENTATIVE provider-native forms, not verified tool output. Stage 3 (SCIP) and Stage 5 (LSP) must re-verify against real provider payloads before relying on them.

F1 RESOLVED (owner decision 2026-08-03): Variant C, precision-aware overload_identity. The heuristic tier commits arity only (signature_precision=arity_only, signature_key=null); the exact tier adds the typed signature. Stable unit identity anchors on the core key, not the typed hash. See reports/024, section 'F1 Resolution — Variant C'. Same-arity disambiguation (F1a) is an open Stage 1 arbitration rule.

2026-08-28 (Stage 1): each distinct_facts_must_not_merge entry gained a structured expected_canonical_key. This restates the claim the prose already made so the fixture can be executed as a golden test instead of read by hand; no claim was changed.

expected_canonical_key.note: Variant C: unit identity anchors on core_key (owner, symbol, arity[, same-arity ordinal]). signature_precision=typed with signature_key is the exact-tier REFINEMENT; a regex-only repo yields signature_precision=arity_only, signature_key=null on the same core_key.

normalization_obligations: Variant C (owner decision 2026-08-03): overload_identity is precision-aware, not one fixed string.
Heuristic tier (regex/tree-sitter) emits signature_precision=arity_only, signature_key=null; it must NOT guess parameter types.
Exact tier (SCIP/LSP) emits signature_precision=typed with a fully-qualified, type-only signature_key (return type excluded, parameter names excluded).
Stable unit identity anchors on the core key (owner, symbol, arity[, same-arity ordinal]); the typed signature is refining evidence, not part of the unit_id.
Same-arity overloads (F1a) require an explicit Stage 1 arbitration rule; arity alone does not disambiguate them.

distinct_facts_must_not_merge.reason: arity 2 vs arity 1 for the same method name; distinct overload.

expected_canonical_overload_identity.note: Distinct core_key from arity 1; heuristic tier separates it by arity alone, no ambiguity.

distinct_facts_must_not_merge.reason: different method name and a generic parameter type; distinct symbol.

different owner/symbol; MUST NOT collide even though its regex signature hash (sig5e75e42b) is byte-identical to handle(String). A hash-only merge key would be unsafe; the canonical key must include owner+symbol+path, not only the signature hash.
